title: Fresh-seed review (57) of c43's CIPS consumer, with the X twin and E fork run: prey divide only with consumers (112 vs 1 strict splits) and every consumer dissolves within 100 t of the prey cut (35 -> 0, fed run 30-35), but consumers are caps on prey droplets (91% of consumer bodies touch prey, 57% of their area inside it) that divide jointly with their prey (2 strict consumer splits); Weak on I and D for the consumer
summary: Re-ran the claimed world unchanged on seed 57 (labkit, 120 frames, t=12000, --lineage-k 5), its consumer-free twin (pred_on 0) and the E fork (tcut 3000, 40 frames). From noise, prey droplets (cyan) and consumer bands (cream) form by t=500 and coexist to the end (consumers 27-40, prey 33-65). X: the twin is a frozen emulsion of 75 prey with 1 strict prey split (splits3.py) and 1 labkit persistent split, against 112 strict prey splits and 76 labkit persistent splits (generation 9) with consumers. E: at t=3000 the fork removes all prey; consumers 35 -> 0 by t=3100 and max q falls from 1.01 to the bath 0.08-0.15, while the fed run keeps 30-35 consumers at t=3100-3900. The consumer's dependence on prey is dynamical (q is conserved and never made from prey). But contact.py finds 358 of 393 consumer bodies (0.91) touching a prey droplet within 2 px and on average 57% of a consumer's own area inside prey: they are caps on prey droplets (strip_ch1.png), not separate bodies. labkit counts 30 consumer persistent splits (generation 3), but the strict strip test counts 2 consumer splits on this seed, both joint with a prey droplet that pinches.

seeds_run.result: S, X, E pass; consumer I and D weak: consumers are caps on prey (contact.txt 0.91 touching, 57% area overlap), 2 strict consumer splits (joint with prey) vs 30 labkit persistent splits

verdicts.limitation: Whether a consumer is an individual is the crux: on this seed consumers are bands or caps on prey droplets, partly inside them, and divide only when their prey droplet pinches, so the dividing unit looks like a prey-consumer composite rather than two interacting populations. The E fork removes all prey at once; a local cut of one prey droplet would test whether a single consumer depends on its own prey. One seed; I did not vary dt or dx.
